blocks.text: 1. Citation Prompting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-176849734.png
Context Injection's closing recap pointed forward here. Citation Prompting covers how to instruct the model to reference its sources, putting the labels from context injection to actual use.
It covers writing instructions that make the model point back to specific chunks when it answers.
2. From Injection To Attribution
Context Injection already gave each chunk a visible number or label.
Citation prompting instructs the model to actually use those labels when it answers.
3. Why Citations Matter In RAG Systems

blocks.alt: Why Citations Matter In RAG Systems
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-223862022.png
System Prompting covered grounding the response in retrieved context; a citation lets a user verify a claim against its actual source.
This turns a confident sounding answer into a checkable one.
4. Explicit Citation Instructions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-268137969.png
Simply providing labeled sources is not enough on its own.
The system prompt needs to explicitly require citing the source label after every claim.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Result"],"rows":[["Labeled sources, no explicit instruction","Model may not cite consistently, or at all"],["Labeled sources plus explicit citation requirement","Model reliably cites its sources"]]}

blocks.text: 5. Citation Format Consistency
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-760041922.png
Specifying an exact citation format, like bracketed numbers, keeps citations parseable and consistent.
A predictable format lets downstream code extract and verify citations programmatically.
6. Handling Claims Without A Source
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-79982706.png
System Prompting covered handling missing information explicitly; the model similarly needs guidance for claims it cannot trace back to a specific chunk.
It should be instructed to avoid making claims it cannot cite, rather than citing loosely.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An instruction like "only make claims you can cite with a source label" discourages the model from blending uncited general knowledge into an otherwise well grounded, cited response.

blocks.text: 7. Verifying Citations Programmatically
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581124-156314253.png
After the model responds, code can check whether every cited label actually exists in the injected context.
This catches hallucinated citations that reference a source number that was never actually provided.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A response citing "[source: 5]" when only four sources were injected into the context signals a hallucinated citation that programmatic verification can catch and flag automatically.

blocks.text: 8. Citations Do Not Guarantee Accuracy
A model can still cite a real source while misrepresenting what that source actually says.
Citation prompting improves traceability, but does not by itself guarantee correctness.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Property","What citation prompting provides"],"rows":[["Traceability","A citation lets a claim be traced back to its source"],["Accuracy","Not guaranteed; the citation could still misrepresent the source"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Citation Prompting Deserves Dedicated Instructions

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Citation Prompting Deserves Dedicated Instructions
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581443-156120552.png
Systems where users need to verify claims need citation prompting.
Casual, low stakes conversational use, by contrast, may not need explicit citation requirements.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates verifying that every citation in a model response references an actually injected source.

code.content:
injected_sources = {1: "handbook_v3", 2: "faq_page"}

model_response = "Refunds take five business days [source: 1]. Damaged items are covered [source: 2]. Extended warranties apply too [source: 3]."

import re

def extract_citations(response):
    return [int(match) for match in re.findall(r"\[source: (\d+)\]", response)]

def verify_citations(response, injected_sources):
    # check each cited label against the sources actually injected
    cited = extract_citations(response)
    valid = [c for c in cited if c in injected_sources]
    hallucinated = [c for c in cited if c not in injected_sources]
    return valid, hallucinated

valid, hallucinated = verify_citations(model_response, injected_sources)
print(f"Injected sources: {injected_sources}")
print(f"Valid citations: {valid}")
print(f"Hallucinated citations: {hallucinated}")

if hallucinated:
    print("\nWarning: the response cited a source that was never actually provided.")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the response citing source 3, which was never injected into the context, exactly the kind of hallucinated citation risk that programmatic verification is designed to catch.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Providing labeled sources without an explicit instruction requiring the model to cite them.
Using an inconsistent citation format that downstream code cannot reliably parse.
Never programmatically verifying that cited sources actually exist in the injected context.
Assuming a cited response is automatically accurate rather than just traceable.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Citation prompting instructs the model to reference specific source labels when it answers.
It puts the numbered or labeled chunks from context injection to actual use.
Citations let a user verify a claim against its actual source, making answers checkable.
The system prompt needs to explicitly require citing sources; labels alone are not enough.
A consistent citation format lets downstream code extract and verify citations reliably.
The model should avoid making claims it cannot trace back to a cited source.
Code can programmatically check whether every cited source actually exists in the context.
Citations improve traceability but do not by themselves guarantee the claim is accurate.
